title: The cost of being half-hearted in AI and how to avoid the Solow Paradox
excerpt: Why a lot of projects don’t deliver ROI, and how enterprises can tackle it
content_html:
Not too long ago, one of the world's most data-driven companies admitted that its AI spending was becoming “harder to justify”. Uber's President and COO, Andrew Macdonald, told the Rapid Response podcast that the company had blown through its entire 2026 AI budget in roughly four months, with around 5,000 engineers leaning on Anthropic's Claude Code.

Uber isn’t alone. Forrester research found that enterprises are deferring around 25% of planned AI spend to 2027, as CFO scrutiny over ROI intensifies. And McKinsey's State of AI report summarized that while 62% of companies are experimenting with AI agents, only 23% have scaled them in even a single business function.

CEO at Nearform.

While these may look like the statistics of a technology that isn't working, they’re actually the statistics of a technology being used in the wrong way.

If we rewind back to 1987, Nobel laureate economist, Robert Solow, observed something that many at the time really resonated with: “You can see the computer age everywhere but in the productivity statistics.” Computers were everywhere across the innovative businesses that had invested heavily in them, but the productivity numbers didn’t move.

The returns only materialized years later, once organizations stopped bolting computers onto old processes and started fundamentally redesigning how they worked.

Many executives, alongside Uber’s COO, are at exactly that inflection point with AI - people are using it, running out of budgets to maintain usage, and at the same time, not really seeing the productivity boost they were hoping for.

This is the Solow Paradox repeating its course, which begs the question: will enterprises learn from previous mistakes?

The flatline behind the hype

There’s a critical distinction that most enterprise leaders are still failing to make: AI activity is not the same as AI maturity. You can run 40 pilots, adopt six platforms and report impressive usage statistics, and still be no closer to measurable business value.

Uber found this out in painful, public fashion, and has since openly questioned whether the rising cost of AI token usage is translating into proportional productivity gains. What makes Uber's situation instructive is not just the financial exposure, but how the organization approached adoption. Internal leaderboards were introduced to rank teams by AI tool usage, with the incentive being to use more tools.

The outcome was more usage, but the business impact slowly became harder to justify.

This is what happens when you gamify adoption without redesigning the workflows underneath it. You optimize the tool usage metric, not the business outcome. Uber has now joined several other top organizations, including Microsoft, Meta and Amazon, in capping AI usage to tackle the issue.

What’s interesting here is that when AI token usage is unconstrained, activity becomes the proxy for progress, but when it’s capped, organizations are forced to confront a harder question: what is each token actually producing?

In that sense, token spend behaves like an economic mirror. It scales immediately with adoption, while productivity only improves when workflows are redesigned. The gap between the two is where most AI ROI disappears.

The real culprit: Individual task optimization

When AI tools are deployed at the individual level, they tend to optimize the task, not the workflow.

A developer writes code faster, a marketer drafts copy in a fraction of the time, or a data analyst generates a summary report in minutes rather than hours.

All of these examples are real gains, but if the code still sits in a review queue for four days, if the draft still passes through three rounds of manual approval, or if the report still requires someone to manually transfer it into a decision-making dashboard - the time saved will pool at the next bottleneck.

Individual productivity gains that don’t translate into workflow redesign don’t compound. They stagnate, and this is the core of the maturity gap. AI maturity isn't about how many tools you've adopted, or how many pilots you've launched. It's about whether you've moved consistently from opportunity to outcome.

That shift requires a fundamentally different way of working.

Now, the term ‘production-ready AI’ gets used loosely. It’s worth being precise about what it actually means in practice, because most enterprise AI deployments fall short of the bar.

Production-ready AI has four characteristics. First, the output feeds directly into a downstream decision or action without manual transfer. It’s embedded in the workflow, not adjacent to it.

Second, the system has clearly defined failure modes, so the organization knows exactly what happens when the AI gets something wrong, and who’s accountable for remedying it. Third, there’s a named owner responsible for performance, adoption and iteration. Finally, and most critically, the surrounding process has been redesigned - not merely augmented.

The framework that closes the gap

So, how can businesses make this shift in practice? The answer is maintaining disciplined execution.

One way to build that discipline is a structured cadence we call the 3-3-3 framework: three days to prioritize, three weeks to prove value, and three months to launch a first release. The logic is deceptively simple and deliberately structured.

In the prioritization phase, the question is not “what can AI do?”, it’s “which specific opportunity, tied to a specific business outcome, has the right combination of value, feasibility, data readiness, and organizational sponsorship to pursue right now?”

That focus alone eliminates a significant proportion of AI initiatives that consume resources without clear purpose. It’s the antidote to the open-ended experimentation that left Uber burning through its budget before April was out.

In the proof phase, the focus is validation - not in technical terms, but in commercial ones. Can this solution create measurable value for users and for the business? A proof of concept that demonstrates technical possibility without demonstrating business value isn’t a proof of concept, it’s a prototype without a destination.

In the launch phase, the solution moves into a real environment. It integrates with existing systems, gets adopted by the people it was built for and gets measured against the outcome it was designed to improve. Not against token usage and not against adoption rates.

This rhythm isn’t a rigid formula, however. The shape of the work always depends on the business problem, the data environment, the technical complexity and the organization's appetite for change. What the framework provides is momentum and the discipline to keep that momentum anchored in value.

Shifting from adoption metrics to outcome metrics

The most consequential change enterprise leaders can make right now is a measurement decision.

Enterprises that are serious about closing the gap between AI activity and business impact need to make three shifts. The first is from tool deployment to operating model redesign. Rolling out AI tools is table stakes but building a repeatable operating model - a structured path from idea to proof to scale - is the competitive differentiator.

The second shift is from adoption metrics to outcome metrics. Usage rates, logins and token volumes tell you whether people are using the tools, but they don’t tell you whether the tools are working. Define success in business terms from the outset: cost reduction, time-to-decision, revenue impact, customer satisfaction, and build your measurement framework around those outcomes.

The third shift is from centralized experimentation to distributed accountability. The AI factory model - where a central operating model connects business priorities with delivery, adoption and value measurement - works precisely because it distributes accountability across the organization. Every initiative starts with a clear owner, a clear problem and a clear definition of what success looks like.

Winning the AI day

The productivity paradox Solow identified in 1987 eventually resolved itself. Not because computers got better - though they did - but because organizations learned to reorganize work around the technology, rather than fitting the technology around old ways of working.

The same resolution is available to enterprises deploying AI today. But it requires leaders to make a deliberate choice - to stop measuring success in terms of how many tools have been adopted and start measuring it in terms of how many outcomes have been delivered.

The organizations that win the AI era will not necessarily be those with the largest number of pilots, but rather the ones that build the maturity to turn the right ideas into value and then scale that value with confidence.

That kind of maturity doesn’t happen by accident. It requires structure, discipline and the willingness to ask harder questions about what AI is actually delivering, and what it’s not.

blocks.html_en: Now, the term ‘production-ready AI’ gets used loosely. It’s worth being precise about what it actually means in practice, because most enterprise AI deployments fall short of the bar.

sentences.en: Now, the term ‘production-ready AI’ gets used loosely.
sentences.zh: 现在，“生产就绪的人工智能”一词被广泛使用。

sentences.en: It’s worth being precise about what it actually means in practice, because most enterprise AI deployments fall short of the bar.
sentences.zh: 有必要准确说明它在实践中的实际含义，因为大多数企业人工智能部署都达不到标准。

blocks.html_en: Production-ready AI has four characteristics. First, the output feeds directly into a downstream decision or action without manual transfer. It’s embedded in the workflow, not adjacent to it.

sentences.en: Production-ready AI has four characteristics.
sentences.zh: 生产就绪型人工智能具有四个特征。

sentences.en: First, the output feeds directly into a downstream decision or action without manual transfer.
sentences.zh: 首先，输出直接反馈到下游决策或行动，无需手动传输。

sentences.en: It’s embedded in the workflow, not adjacent to it.
sentences.zh: 它嵌入在工作流程中，而不是与之相邻。

blocks.html_en: Second, the system has clearly defined failure modes, so the organization knows exactly what happens when the AI gets something wrong, and who’s accountable for remedying it. Third, there’s a named owner responsible for performance, adoption and iteration. Finally, and most critically, the surrounding process has been redesigned - not merely augmented.

sentences.en: Second, the system has clearly defined failure modes, so the organization knows exactly what happens when the AI gets something wrong, and who’s accountable for remedying it.
sentences.zh: 其次，该系统具有明确定义的故障模式，因此组织可以准确地知道人工智能出现问题时会发生什么，以及谁负责纠正错误。

sentences.en: Third, there’s a named owner responsible for performance, adoption and iteration.
sentences.zh: 第三，有一个指定的所有者负责性能、采用和迭代。

sentences.en: Finally, and most critically, the surrounding process has been redesigned - not merely augmented.
sentences.zh: 最后，也是最关键的是，周围的流程已经被重新设计——而不仅仅是增强。

blocks.html_en: The framework that closes the gap

sentences.en: The framework that closes the gap
sentences.zh: 缩小差距的框架

blocks.html_en: So, how can businesses make this shift in practice? The answer is maintaining disciplined execution.

sentences.en: So, how can businesses make this shift in practice?
sentences.zh: 那么，企业如何在实践中实现这一转变呢？

sentences.en: The answer is maintaining disciplined execution.
sentences.zh: 答案是保持严格的执行力。

blocks.html_en: One way to build that discipline is a structured cadence we call the 3-3-3 framework: three days to prioritize, three weeks to prove value, and three months to launch a first release. The logic is deceptively simple and deliberately structured.

sentences.en: One way to build that discipline is a structured cadence we call the 3-3-3 framework: three days to prioritize, three weeks to prove value, and three months to launch a first release.
sentences.zh: 建立这种纪律的一种方法是结构化节奏，我们称之为 3-3-3 框架：三天确定优先级，三周证明价值，三个月启动第一个版本。

sentences.en: The logic is deceptively simple and deliberately structured.
sentences.zh: 其逻辑看似简单，而且结构严谨。

blocks.html_en: In the prioritization phase, the question is not “what can AI do?”, it’s “which specific opportunity, tied to a specific business outcome, has the right combination of value, feasibility, data readiness, and organizational sponsorship to pursue right now?”

sentences.en: In the prioritization phase, the question is not “what can AI do?”, it’s “which specific opportunity, tied to a specific business outcome, has the right combination of value, feasibility, data readiness, and organizational sponsorship to pursue right now?”
sentences.zh: 在优先级确定阶段，问题不是“人工智能能做什么？”，而是“与特定业务成果相关的特定机会，具有价值、可行性、数据就绪性和组织赞助的正确组合，可以立即追求？”

blocks.html_en: That focus alone eliminates a significant proportion of AI initiatives that consume resources without clear purpose. It’s the antidote to the open-ended experimentation that left Uber burning through its budget before April was out.

sentences.en: That focus alone eliminates a significant proportion of AI initiatives that consume resources without clear purpose.
sentences.zh: 仅这一重点就消除了很大一部分在没有明确目的的情况下消耗资源的人工智能计划。

sentences.en: It’s the antidote to the open-ended experimentation that left Uber burning through its budget before April was out.
sentences.zh: 这是对开放式实验的解药，该实验导致 Uber 在 4 月份结束之前就耗尽了预算。

blocks.html_en: In the proof phase, the focus is validation - not in technical terms, but in commercial ones. Can this solution create measurable value for users and for the business? A proof of concept that demonstrates technical possibility without demonstrating business value isn’t a proof of concept, it’s a prototype without a destination.

sentences.en: In the proof phase, the focus is validation - not in technical terms, but in commercial ones.
sentences.zh: 在证明阶段，重点是验证——不是技术术语，而是商业术语。

sentences.en: Can this solution create measurable value for users and for the business?
sentences.zh: 该解决方案能否为用户和企业创造可衡量的价值？

sentences.en: A proof of concept that demonstrates technical possibility without demonstrating business value isn’t a proof of concept, it’s a prototype without a destination.
sentences.zh: 展示技术可能性而不展示商业价值的概念证明不是概念证明，而是没有目的地的原型。

blocks.html_en: In the launch phase, the solution moves into a real environment. It integrates with existing systems, gets adopted by the people it was built for and gets measured against the outcome it was designed to improve. Not against token usage and not against adoption rates.

sentences.en: In the launch phase, the solution moves into a real environment.
sentences.zh: 在启动阶段，解决方案将进入真实环境。

sentences.en: It integrates with existing systems, gets adopted by the people it was built for and gets measured against the outcome it was designed to improve.
sentences.zh: 它与现有系统集成，被其构建对象所采用，并根据其旨在改进的结果进行衡量。

sentences.en: Not against token usage and not against adoption rates.
sentences.zh: 不反对代币的使用，也不反对采用率。

blocks.html_en: This rhythm isn’t a rigid formula, however. The shape of the work always depends on the business problem, the data environment, the technical complexity and the organization's appetite for change. What the framework provides is momentum and the discipline to keep that momentum anchored in value.

sentences.en: This rhythm isn’t a rigid formula, however.
sentences.zh: 然而，这种节奏并不是一个严格的公式。

sentences.en: The shape of the work always depends on the business problem, the data environment, the technical complexity and the organization's appetite for change.
sentences.zh: 工作的形式始终取决于业务问题、数据环境、技术复杂性和组织对变革的兴趣。

sentences.zh: 该框架提供的是动力以及将这种动力锚定在价值上的纪律。

blocks.html_en: Shifting from adoption metrics to outcome metrics

sentences.en: Shifting from adoption metrics to outcome metrics

blocks.html_en: The most consequential change enterprise leaders can make right now is a measurement decision.

sentences.en: The most consequential change enterprise leaders can make right now is a measurement decision.
sentences.zh: 企业领导者现在可以做出的最重要的改变是衡量决策。

blocks.html_en: Enterprises that are serious about closing the gap between AI activity and business impact need to make three shifts. The first is from tool deployment to operating model redesign. Rolling out AI tools is table stakes but building a repeatable operating model - a structured path from idea to proof to scale - is the competitive differentiator.

sentences.en: Enterprises that are serious about closing the gap between AI activity and business impact need to make three shifts.
sentences.zh: 认真缩小人工智能活动和业务影响之间差距的企业需要做出三个转变。

sentences.en: The first is from tool deployment to operating model redesign.
sentences.zh: 首先是从工具部署到运营模式重新设计。

sentences.en: Rolling out AI tools is table stakes but building a repeatable operating model - a structured path from idea to proof to scale - is the competitive differentiator.
sentences.zh: 推出人工智能工具是赌注，但建立可重复的运营模型——从想法到验证再到规模化的结构化路径——才是竞争优势。

blocks.html_en: The second shift is from adoption metrics to outcome metrics. Usage rates, logins and token volumes tell you whether people are using the tools, but they don’t tell you whether the tools are working. Define success in business terms from the outset: cost reduction, time-to-decision, revenue impact, customer satisfaction, and build your measurement framework around those outcomes.

sentences.en: The second shift is from adoption metrics to outcome metrics.
sentences.zh: 第二个转变是从采用指标到结果指标。

sentences.en: Usage rates, logins and token volumes tell you whether people are using the tools, but they don’t tell you whether the tools are working.
sentences.zh: 使用率、登录次数和代币数量可以告诉您人们是否正在使用这些工具，但它们并不能告诉您这些工具是否有效。

sentences.en: Define success in business terms from the outset: cost reduction, time-to-decision, revenue impact, customer satisfaction, and build your measurement framework around those outcomes.
sentences.zh: 从一开始就用业务术语定义成功：成本降低、决策时间、收入影响、客户满意度，并围绕这些结果构建衡量框架。

blocks.html_en: The third shift is from centralized experimentation to distributed accountability. The AI factory model - where a central operating model connects business priorities with delivery, adoption and value measurement - works precisely because it distributes accountability across the organization. Every initiative starts with a clear owner, a clear problem and a clear definition of what success looks like.

sentences.en: The third shift is from centralized experimentation to distributed accountability.
sentences.zh: 第三个转变是从集中式实验到分布式问责。

sentences.en: The AI factory model - where a central operating model connects business priorities with delivery, adoption and value measurement - works precisely because it distributes accountability across the organization.
sentences.zh: 人工智能工厂模型——其中一个中央运营模型将业务优先级与交付、采用和价值衡量联系起来——之所以能够精确地发挥作用，是因为它在整个组织中分配了责任。

sentences.en: Every initiative starts with a clear owner, a clear problem and a clear definition of what success looks like.
sentences.zh: 每项举措都始于明确的所有者、明确的问题以及成功的明确定义。

blocks.html_en: The productivity paradox Solow identified in 1987 eventually resolved itself. Not because computers got better - though they did - but because organizations learned to reorganize work around the technology, rather than fitting the technology around old ways of working.

blocks.html_en: The same resolution is available to enterprises deploying AI today. But it requires leaders to make a deliberate choice - to stop measuring success in terms of how many tools have been adopted and start measuring it in terms of how many outcomes have been delivered.

sentences.en: The same resolution is available to enterprises deploying AI today.

blocks.html_en: The organizations that win the AI era will not necessarily be those with the largest number of pilots, but rather the ones that build the maturity to turn the right ideas into value and then scale that value with confidence.

blocks.html_en: CEO at Nearform.

sentences.en: CEO at Nearform.
sentences.zh: Nearform 首席执行官。

content_html_zh:
不久前，世界上最受数据驱动的公司之一承认，其人工智能支出正变得“越来越难以证明其合理性”。 Uber 总裁兼首席运营官 Andrew Macdonald 在 Rapid Response 播客中表示，该公司在大约四个月内就用完了 2026 年的全部人工智能预算，大约 5,000 名工程师依靠 Anthropic 的 Claude Code。

优步并不孤单。 Forrester 研究发现，随着首席财务官对投资回报率的审查力度加大，企业将大约 25% 的人工智能支出计划推迟到 2027 年。 麦肯锡的人工智能现状报告总结称，虽然 62% 的公司正在试验人工智能代理，但只有 23% 的公司在单一业务功能中对其进行了扩展。

Nearform 首席执行官。

虽然这些看起来像是一项不起作用的技术的统计数据，但它们实际上是一项以错误方式使用的技术的统计数据。

如果我们回到 1987 年，诺贝尔经济学奖得主罗伯特·索洛 (Robert Solow) 观察到了当时许多人真正产生共鸣的一句话：“你可以在任何地方看到计算机时代，但在生产力统计数据中却找不到。” 在投入巨资的创新企业中，计算机无处不在，但生产力数字却没有变化。

几年后，当组织停止将计算机固定在旧流程上并开始从根本上重新设计其工作方式时，回报才得以实现。

许多高管，以及 Uber 的首席运营官，都正处于人工智能的拐点——人们正在使用它，用尽了维持使用的预算，同时，并没有真正看到他们所希望的生产力提升。

这是索洛悖论的重演，这就引出了一个问题：企业会从以前的错误中吸取教训吗？

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

炒作背后的平淡

大多数企业领导者仍然未能区分一个关键的区别：人工智能活动与人工智能成熟度不同。 您可以运行 40 个试点、采用 6 个平台并报告令人印象深刻的使用统计数据，但仍然无法接近可衡量的业务价值。

Uber 以痛苦的公开方式发现了这一点，此后公开质疑人工智能代币使用成本的上升是否会转化为成比例的生产力收益。 Uber 的情况之所以具有启发性，不仅在于其财务风险，还在于该组织如何采用该技术。 引入了内部排行榜，根据人工智能工具的使用情况对团队进行排名，以激励使用更多工具。

结果是使用量增加，但业务影响慢慢变得越来越难以证明。

当您将采用游戏化而不重新设计其下面的工作流程时，就会发生这种情况。 您优化的是工具使用指标，而不是业务成果。 Uber 现在已与微软、Meta 和亚马逊等其他几家顶级组织一起限制人工智能的使用，以解决这一问题。

这里有趣的是，当人工智能代币的使用不受限制时，活动就成为进步的代表，但当它受到限制时，组织被迫面对一个更难的问题：每个代币实际生产什么？

从这个意义上说，代币支出就像一面经济镜子。 它会随着采用而立即扩展，而只有重新设计工作流程才能提高生产力。 两者之间的差距是大多数人工智能投资回报率消失的地方。

真正的罪魁祸首：个人任务优化

当人工智能工具部署在个人层面时，它们往往会优化任务，而不是工作流程。

开发人员可以更快地编写代码，营销人员可以在很短的时间内起草副本，或者数据分析师可以在几分钟而不是几小时内生成摘要报告。

所有这些例子都是真正的收获，但如果代码仍然在审查队列中等待四天，如果草案仍然经过三轮手动批准，或者报告仍然需要有人将其手动传输到决策仪表板中 - 节省的时间将汇集到下一个瓶颈。

个人生产力的提高如果不转化为工作流程的重新设计，就不会产生复合效应。 他们停滞不前，这就是成熟度差距的核心。 人工智能成熟度与您采用了多少工具或启动了多少试点无关。 关键在于你是否始终如一地从机会走向结果。

这种转变需要一种根本不同的工作方式。

现在，“生产就绪的人工智能”一词被广泛使用。 有必要准确说明它在实践中的实际含义，因为大多数企业人工智能部署都达不到标准。

生产就绪型人工智能具有四个特征。 首先，输出直接反馈到下游决策或行动，无需手动传输。 它嵌入在工作流程中，而不是与之相邻。

其次，该系统具有明确定义的故障模式，因此组织可以准确地知道人工智能出现问题时会发生什么，以及谁负责纠正错误。 第三，有一个指定的所有者负责性能、采用和迭代。 最后，也是最关键的是，周围的流程已经被重新设计——而不仅仅是增强。

缩小差距的框架

那么，企业如何在实践中实现这一转变呢？ 答案是保持严格的执行力。

建立这种纪律的一种方法是结构化节奏，我们称之为 3-3-3 框架：三天确定优先级，三周证明价值，三个月启动第一个版本。 其逻辑看似简单，而且结构严谨。

在优先级确定阶段，问题不是“人工智能能做什么？”，而是“与特定业务成果相关的特定机会，具有价值、可行性、数据就绪性和组织赞助的正确组合，可以立即追求？”

仅这一重点就消除了很大一部分在没有明确目的的情况下消耗资源的人工智能计划。 这是对开放式实验的解药，该实验导致 Uber 在 4 月份结束之前就耗尽了预算。

在证明阶段，重点是验证——不是技术术语，而是商业术语。 该解决方案能否为用户和企业创造可衡量的价值？ 展示技术可能性而不展示商业价值的概念证明不是概念证明，而是没有目的地的原型。

在启动阶段，解决方案将进入真实环境。 它与现有系统集成，被其构建对象所采用，并根据其旨在改进的结果进行衡量。 不反对代币的使用，也不反对采用率。

然而，这种节奏并不是一个严格的公式。 工作的形式始终取决于业务问题、数据环境、技术复杂性和组织对变革的兴趣。 该框架提供的是动力以及将这种动力锚定在价值上的纪律。

从采用指标转向结果指标

企业领导者现在可以做出的最重要的改变是衡量决策。

认真缩小人工智能活动和业务影响之间差距的企业需要做出三个转变。 首先是从工具部署到运营模式重新设计。 推出人工智能工具是赌注，但建立可重复的运营模型——从想法到验证再到规模化的结构化路径——才是竞争优势。

第二个转变是从采用指标到结果指标。 使用率、登录次数和代币数量可以告诉您人们是否正在使用这些工具，但它们并不能告诉您这些工具是否有效。 从一开始就用业务术语定义成功：成本降低、决策时间、收入影响、客户满意度，并围绕这些结果构建衡量框架。

第三个转变是从集中式实验到分布式问责。 人工智能工厂模型——其中一个中央运营模型将业务优先级与交付、采用和价值衡量联系起来——之所以能够精确地发挥作用，是因为它在整个组织中分配了责任。 每项举措都始于明确的所有者、明确的问题以及成功的明确定义。

赢得人工智能日

索洛在 1987 年发现的生产力悖论最终自行解决。 并不是因为计算机变得更好了——尽管确实如此——而是因为组织学会了围绕技术重新组织工作，而不是让技术适应旧的工作方式。

如今部署人工智能的企业也可以采用同样的解决方案。 但这需要领导者做出深思熟虑的选择——停止以采用了多少工具来衡量成功，而开始以已交付多少成果来衡量成功。

赢得人工智能时代的组织不一定是那些拥有最多试点数量的组织，而是那些建立成熟度以将正确的想法转化为价值，然后充满信心地扩展该价值的组织。

这种成熟并非偶然发生。 它需要结构、纪律，并愿意就人工智能实际提供什么、不提供什么提出更难的问题。
